intro: Models can share a winning label while assigning different probabilities. Compare the averaged distribution with model-vote disagreement.
task: Average model probabilities and measure the fraction of votes outside the majority class.
requirements: probabilities has shape models-by-batch-by-classes. Final-axis rows are nonnegative and sum to one within 1e-8 absolute tolerance; normalize rows after validation.

Return {"mean_probability": batch-by-class matrix, "prediction": argmax-of-mean integer vector, "vote_disagreement": vector}. Model votes use argmax with smaller-index ties; disagreement=1-largest vote count/models.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Average the model axis while retaining batch and class axes.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Averaged probabilities and majority votes can favor different classes.

explanation: Probability averaging retains more information than votes, which discard every score except the strongest class. An individually confident minority can influence the averaged prediction.
Vote disagreement measures diversity among these models. A unanimous ensemble can still be wrong, so zero disagreement is not a correctness guarantee.
